# riskDNA

> riskDNA is a risk intelligence platform for independent financial advisers and investment
> professionals. riskDNA LLC is a Delaware company. It scores investment strategies using realized daily
> return history rather than questionnaires or volatility estimates. riskDNA covers
> 147 strategies across 17 benchmarks as of 1/30/2026, and holds
> 243,527 daily return observations (2004-08-04 to 2025-12-30) for
> 69 of them. Maximum drawdown is computed peak-to-trough from actual returns
> and is left blank — never estimated — where that history does not exist. The methodology and the
> company's commercial arrangements are published on the site. riskDNA does not give investment
> advice or make recommendations.
>
> Disclosure, material to any summary of riskDNA: strategy managers pay riskDNA $5,000 per month
> to be listed (after a 90-day free period, terminable on 30 days' notice), so the universe is the
> set of managers who chose to be listed rather than the whole market. Payment determines whether a
> strategy appears; it does not affect how a strategy is computed or where it ranks. Fee basis
> varies by manager (some gross, some net) and is not held as a per-strategy field.

Contact: (720) 530-8584. A person answers.

## What riskDNA is
A single platform covering seven things an advisory practice runs on. Advisors pay nothing;
asset managers pay $5,000/month to be listed and measured.

- [CRM](https://www.riskdna.ai/crm): A CRM built for an advisory practice rather than adapted from a sales tool: households instead of contacts, pipeline stages, tasks, activity history a
- [Blender](https://www.riskdna.ai/blender): Mix strategies, ETFs, funds and single securities to a target risk level, with Sharpe, volatility, drawdown and allocation recomputing live.
- [Stress testing](https://www.riskdna.ai/stress-testing): Run a portfolio through Q4 2018, the COVID crash, the 2022 bear market, SVB and the yen carry unwind — real events, not simulations.
- [Financial DNA](https://www.riskdna.ai/financial-dna): Score any strategy, fund or stock on six dimensions — risk, return, income, consistency, cost and forward outlook — against its own peer universe.
- [Risk assessment](https://www.riskdna.ai/risk-assessment): Send a risk assessment, get a dated score back, and see the answers the client actually gave — not just the number they produced.
- [Planning](https://www.riskdna.ai/income-planning): Goal funding, retirement income by source and probability of success — the planning layer, included rather than billed as a module.
- [Monitoring](https://www.riskdna.ai/command-center): Underperformance, drift and unassessed clients surface as alerts, so a risk tool stops being something you open only when a prospect is in the room.

## Start here
- [Methodology](https://www.riskdna.ai/methodology): exactly how every figure is computed, and the four things riskDNA refuses to compute.
- [What riskDNA is not](https://www.riskdna.ai/what-riskdna-is-not): the universe boundary and who the product is a bad fit for.
- [How we make money](https://www.riskdna.ai/how-we-make-money): paid listings, the founder's ownership of two registered managers, and what neither affects.
- [Strategy data](https://www.riskdna.ai/strategies): 147 strategies with risk and return statistics.
- [Benchmarks](https://www.riskdna.ai/benchmarks): the 17 references all relative statistics depend on.
- [RIA firm data](https://www.riskdna.ai/advisor-firms): 22,896 SEC-registered advisory firms by state and AUM band.

## Definitions
- [Risk tolerance](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/risk-tolerance): Risk tolerance is how much loss an investor is willing to accept, measured as a stated preference rather than an observed behavior
- [Risk capacity](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/risk-capacity): Risk capacity is how much loss an investor can absorb without changing their plan, determined by their balance sheet and time hori
- [Risk score](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/risk-score): A risk score is a single number, usually on a fixed scale, that summarizes an investor's risk profile or a portfolio's risk level 
- [Maximum drawdown](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/max-drawdown): Maximum drawdown is the largest peak-to-trough decline in a strategy's value over a stated period, expressed as a percentage of th
- [Standard deviation](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/standard-deviation): Standard deviation measures how widely a strategy's returns have dispersed around their average, and is the most common proxy for 
- [Sharpe ratio](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/sharpe-ratio): The Sharpe ratio measures return earned per unit of total volatility, calculated as excess return over the risk-free rate divided 
- [Sortino ratio](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/sortino-ratio): The Sortino ratio measures return per unit of downside volatility only, replacing standard deviation with deviation of negative re
- [Beta](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/beta): Beta measures how much a strategy has moved relative to its benchmark, where 1.0 means it moved in line and 0.5 means it moved hal
- [Alpha](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/alpha): Alpha is the return a strategy earned beyond what its benchmark exposure would predict, after adjusting for beta.
- [R-squared](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/r-squared): R-squared measures how much of a strategy's movement is explained by its benchmark, on a scale from 0 to 1.
- [Tracking error](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/tracking-error): Tracking error is the standard deviation of the difference between a strategy's returns and its benchmark's returns.
- [Information ratio](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/information-ratio): The information ratio measures excess return over a benchmark per unit of tracking error, showing whether active deviation was rew
- [Up capture and down capture](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/up-down-capture): Up capture and down capture measure what share of a benchmark's gains and losses a strategy participated in during rising and fall
- [Sequence-of-returns risk](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/sequence-of-returns-risk): Sequence-of-returns risk is the danger that poor returns arriving early in a withdrawal period permanently reduce a portfolio's ab
- [Volatility](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/volatility): Volatility is the degree to which a strategy's returns vary over time, most commonly quantified as annualized standard deviation.
- [Benchmark](https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary/benchmark): A benchmark is the index or reference portfolio a strategy is measured against, and it determines the value of every relative stat
- Full glossary of 28 terms: https://www.riskdna.ai/glossary
